{"content":"### Root Cause

Session JSONL files grew without bound from the append-only `custom` ledgers, and `fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` even though the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Two write-side defects fed the growth: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, with only the latest snapshot ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run now PROJECTS the rewrite — `bytesAfter` is the byte sum of the kept spans (header + survivors + latest keep-latest snapshots, exactly what pass 2 streams), and the report tracks dropped bytes per ledger type (`reclaimed 855.7 MB: model_request_summary×…, …`). Dry-run size lines read `X → Y (projected)`.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` — a clock-seamed write-time window (30 s) for latest-snapshot-wins ledgers, same tracker shape as the CLI liveness trackers (production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ field in `agent_cli.dart`): `_persistJobBoard` consults the throttle — the first board mutation in a window appends; the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush. Empty boards never append (no `[]` snapshots in no-job sessions). The throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush the final state and disarm the leg; run finalize (`_afterRun`) gives an unforced persist chance so per-settle reaction runs don't defeat the coalescing.
- No change to what resume reads: `ShellJobBoard.latestRecords` still rehydrates from the newest snapshot, which now always carries the final terminal states.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart` — dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture; `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes`; per-type accounting + `(projected)` line — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 4 jobs × (start + settle) = 8 board mutations leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` policy: window coalescing, trailing-flush due/re-arm, steady-state reopen, reset, production leg + dispose — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB block texts encodes under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full suite: see CI (local run green across session/trajectory/CLI repair + job-board suites, 88 targeted tests + full `dart test`).

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 sessions (spans are copied byte-for-byte); a torn line with malformed bytes could round differently, but torn lines are kept and repair never deletes what it cannot parse.
- Resume-speed (`boot_stage context` on multi-hundred-MB files), hash-based `model_request_summary` references, and automatic compaction on a size threshold are the ticket's optional items — not touched here (follow-ups).

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. ### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).

- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Session JSONL files grew without bound from the append-only `custom` ledgers, and `fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` even though the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Two write-side defects fed the growth: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, with only the latest snapshot ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run now PROJECTS the rewrite — `bytesAfter` is the byte sum of the kept spans (header + survivors + latest keep-latest snapshots, exactly what pass 2 streams), and the report tracks dropped bytes per ledger type (`reclaimed 855.7 MB: model_request_summary×…, …`). Dry-run size lines read `X → Y (projected)`.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` — a clock-seamed write-time window (30 s) for latest-snapshot-wins ledgers, same tracker shape as the CLI liveness trackers (production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ field in `agent_cli.dart`): `_persistJobBoard` consults the throttle — the first board mutation in a window appends; the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush. Empty boards never append (no `[]` snapshots in no-job sessions). The throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush the final state and disarm the leg; run finalize (`_afterRun`) gives an unforced persist chance so per-settle reaction runs don't defeat the coalescing.
- No change to what resume reads: `ShellJobBoard.latestRecords` still rehydrates from the newest snapshot, which now always carries the final terminal states.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart` — dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture; `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes`; per-type accounting + `(projected)` line — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 4 jobs × (start + settle) = 8 board mutations leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` policy: window coalescing, trailing-flush due/re-arm, steady-state reopen, reset, production leg + dispose — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB block texts encodes under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full suite: see CI (local run green across session/trajectory/CLI repair + job-board suites, 88 targeted tests + full `dart test`).

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 sessions (spans are copied byte-for-byte); a torn line with malformed bytes could round differently, but torn lines are kept and repair never deletes what it cannot parse.
- Resume-speed (`boot_stage context` on multi-hundred-MB files), hash-based `model_request_summary` references, and automatic compaction on a size threshold are the ticket's optional items — not touched here (follow-ups).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Session JSONL files grew without bound from the append-only `custom` ledgers, and `fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` even though the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Two write-side defects fed the growth: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, with only the latest snapshot ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run now PROJECTS the rewrite — `bytesAfter` is the byte sum of the kept spans (header + survivors + latest keep-latest snapshots, exactly what pass 2 streams), and the report tracks dropped bytes per ledger type (`reclaimed 855.7 MB: model_request_summary×…, …`). Dry-run size lines read `X → Y (projected)`.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` — a clock-seamed write-time window (30 s) for latest-snapshot-wins ledgers, same tracker shape as the CLI liveness trackers (production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ field in `agent_cli.dart`): `_persistJobBoard` consults the throttle — the first board mutation in a window appends; the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush. Empty boards never append (no `[]` snapshots in no-job sessions). The throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush the final state and disarm the leg; run finalize (`_afterRun`) gives an unforced persist chance so per-settle reaction runs don't defeat the coalescing.
- No change to what resume reads: `ShellJobBoard.latestRecords` still rehydrates from the newest snapshot, which now always carries the final terminal states.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart` — dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture; `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes`; per-type accounting + `(projected)` line — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 4 jobs × (start + settle) = 8 board mutations leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` policy: window coalescing, trailing-flush due/re-arm, steady-state reopen, reset, production leg + dispose — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB block texts encodes under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full suite: see CI (local run green across session/trajectory/CLI repair + job-board suites, 88 targeted tests + full `dart test`).

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 sessions (spans are copied byte-for-byte); a torn line with malformed bytes could round differently, but torn lines are kept and repair never deletes what it cannot parse.
- Resume-speed (`boot_stage context` on multi-hundred-MB files), hash-based `model_request_summary` references, and automatic compaction on a size threshold are the ticket's optional items — not touched here (follow-ups).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Session JSONL files grew without bound from the append-only `custom` ledgers, and `fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` even though the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Two write-side defects fed the growth: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, with only the latest snapshot ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run now PROJECTS the rewrite — `bytesAfter` is the byte sum of the kept spans (header + survivors + latest keep-latest snapshots, exactly what pass 2 streams), and the report tracks dropped bytes per ledger type (`reclaimed 855.7 MB: model_request_summary×…, …`). Dry-run size lines read `X → Y (projected)`.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` — a clock-seamed write-time window (30 s) for latest-snapshot-wins ledgers, same tracker shape as the CLI liveness trackers (production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ field in `agent_cli.dart`): `_persistJobBoard` consults the throttle — the first board mutation in a window appends; the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush. Empty boards never append (no `[]` snapshots in no-job sessions). The throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush the final state and disarm the leg; run finalize (`_afterRun`) gives an unforced persist chance so per-settle reaction runs don't defeat the coalescing.
- No change to what resume reads: `ShellJobBoard.latestRecords` still rehydrates from the newest snapshot, which now always carries the final terminal states.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart` — dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture; `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes`; per-type accounting + `(projected)` line — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 4 jobs × (start + settle) = 8 board mutations leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` policy: window coalescing, trailing-flush due/re-arm, steady-state reopen, reset, production leg + dispose — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB block texts encodes under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full suite: see CI (local run green across session/trajectory/CLI repair + job-board suites, 88 targeted tests + full `dart test`).

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 sessions (spans are copied byte-for-byte); a torn line with malformed bytes could round differently, but torn lines are kept and repair never deletes what it cannot parse.
- Resume-speed (`boot_stage context` on multi-hundred-MB files), hash-based `model_request_summary` references, and automatic compaction on a size threshold are the ticket's optional items — not touched here (follow-ups).

{"content":"### Root Cause

Session JSONL files grew without bound from the append-only `custom` ledgers, and `fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` even though the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Two write-side defects fed the growth: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, with only the latest snapshot ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run now PROJECTS the rewrite — `bytesAfter` is the byte sum of the kept spans (header + survivors + latest keep-latest snapshots, exactly what pass 2 streams), and the report tracks dropped bytes per ledger type (`reclaimed 855.7 MB: model_request_summary×…, …`). Dry-run size lines read `X → Y (projected)`.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` — a clock-seamed write-time window (30 s) for latest-snapshot-wins ledgers, same tracker shape as the CLI liveness trackers (production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ field in `agent_cli.dart`): `_persistJobBoard` consults the throttle — the first board mutation in a window appends; the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush. Empty boards never append (no `[]` snapshots in no-job sessions). The throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush the final state and disarm the leg; run finalize (`_afterRun`) gives an unforced persist chance so per-settle reaction runs don't defeat the coalescing.
- No change to what resume reads: `ShellJobBoard.latestRecords` still rehydrates from the newest snapshot, which now always carries the final terminal states.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart` — dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture; `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes`; per-type accounting + `(projected)` line — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 4 jobs × (start + settle) = 8 board mutations leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — PASSED (failed before the fix).
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` policy: window coalescing, trailing-flush due/re-arm, steady-state reopen, reset, production leg + dispose — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB block texts encodes under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full suite: see CI (local run green across session/trajectory/CLI repair + job-board suites, 88 targeted tests + full `dart test`).

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 sessions (spans are copied byte-for-byte); a torn line with malformed bytes could round differently, but torn lines are kept and repair never deletes what it cannot parse.
- Resume-speed (`boot_stage context` on multi-hundred-MB files), hash-based `model_request_summary` references, and automatic compaction on a size threshold are the ticket's optional items — not touched here (follow-ups).

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. ### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).

- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

{"content":"### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

{"content":"### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

{"content":"### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.
